question: to the Commission Elena Nevado del Campo (PPE), Isabel Benjumea Benjumea (PPE) Subject:

According to recently published information, during the COVID-19 pandemic, the Government of the Canary Islands awarded several contracts for the purchase of medical equipment worth tens of millions of euros. Some of these contracts are said to have been awarded under an emergency procedure by the current minister, Ángel Víctor Torres, to companies currently under investigation by various judicial bodies – notably the European Public Prosecutor’s Office, the Civil Guard and the Canary Islands Court of Auditors – and co-financed with ERDF funds. The information points to possible irregularities in the processing of certain dossiers, such as shortcomings in the suppliers’ technical solvency accreditation, documentary shortcomings or traceability problems regarding the use of European funds. Considering the important role of the Commission in the protection of the financial interests of the Union: 1.
Does the Commission know whether any of the health contracts awarded in the Canary Islands during the pandemic under investigation were financed, in whole or in part, by ERDF funds?

Has it requested information from the Spanish authorities or carried out verifications to ensure that said funds were used in accordance with the applicable law and the principle of sound financial management?
In the event that irregularities were to be identified in projects financed with EU funds, what measures will be taken to recover the funds?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (21.5.2026) The Commission is aware of the judicial investigations on the health equipment contracts in Canary Islands. In line with the shared management principle governing cohesion policy, the Commission has requested information to the Spanish Managing authorities on the possible support from the European Regional Development Fund (ERDF) funding to these contracts. Member States bear the primary responsibility for the implementation and control of operations funded by the ERDF, including detecting and correcting irregularities. The Spanish authorities are therefore responsible for ensuring that contracts co-financed by ERDF comply with applicable procurement rules and that funds are used correctly. The Commission’s role is supervisory ensuring that the national management and control systems provide the assurance that resources are used in compliance with EU law and the principle of sound financial management. The procurement procedures for the specific contracts in the Canary Islands were not subject to the Commission’s own verification. However, if irregularities were identified, either through national controls or investigations by the European Public Prosecutor’s Office, the Commission would expect the Spanish authorities to take corrective measures, including financial corrections where necessary1. Failing to take action at national level, the Commission would take appropriate action in order to ensure that EU funds are used in accordance with the applicable rules, including through the application of the appropriate financial corrections. The Commission remains in contact with the Spanish authorities. Should new information emerge, the Commission will assess whether further action is required.
1 in line with Article 69 of Regulation (EU) 2021/1060; ELI: http://data.europa.eu/eli/reg/2021/1060/oj.
